result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.radiality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate radiality centrality for each node in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40321-L40400){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.radiality( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Radiality](/assets/graphs/radiality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by radiality, which rises as eccentricity falls. Bridge node E reaches every node within two hops and scores 0.50; C, D and F score 0.33; the outer nodes A, B and G score 0.17." width="100%"} Radiality measures how central a node is based on its eccentricity relative to the graph diameter. The formula is: `radiality(v) = (diameter + 1 - eccentricity(v)) / (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of nodes. Higher radiality indicates a more central position in the network. Radiality compares every node against one graph-wide diameter, so it is only defined for connected graphs; in a disconnected graph every node gets `None`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store radiality values. If `None`, uses `radiality` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to radiality scores. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float | None] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: Dictionary mapping node IDs to radiality scores (`0.0` to `1.0`). Values are `None` for every node if the graph is disconnected. If `return_dict=` is `False` returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub reaches every other node in a single hop, giving it the highest possible radiality, while each leaf -- two hops from any other leaf -- scores lower: ::: {#eab8bbff .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) graph.radiality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.3333333333333333, 1: 0.6666666666666666, 4: 0.3333333333333333, 2: 0.3333333333333333} ``` ::: :::
